# AppearanceControl

`AppearanceControl` lets people choose a Light, Auto or Dark colour scheme for your application. Place it anywhere inside `BreezeProvider`; it reads and updates the provider's appearance, and Auto follows the operating system preference.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Remembering the choice

The control does not save the choice in browser storage. To restore it on the next visit, store the value reported by the provider's `onAppearanceChange` and pass it back as `appearance`.

## Shadows

Shadows change with the selected appearance, along with colours and native controls.

<Canvas of={Stories.ThemeReactiveShadow} />

## Accessibility

The three options form a single-selection group named by the provider's `appearance` message, so screen readers announce which option is selected.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './AttachmentRow.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Shows an attached document or photograph with its visible status and actions."
/>

# AttachmentRow

`AttachmentRow` shows one attached file in a compact row, with its name, type, size, status and actions. Use it to list the files attached to a record.

Pass `filename`, `fileType` (`document` or `photo`), `sizeBytes` and a visible `status` such as `Uploaded` or `Upload failed`. The size is formatted for the `BreezeProvider` locale.

## Documents and photos

Documents show a page preview. Photos show the image passed as `thumbnailUrl`, or a camera placeholder without one; only photos accept `thumbnailUrl`. The file type is also written as text, so the thumbnail is not the only way to tell them apart.

<Canvas of={Stories.Document} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Photo} />

## Actions

Pass `onOpen` to show an **Open** button. To open the file in a `DocumentViewer` with a transition between the two, give both the same `transitionName`.

To add an overflow menu, pass an `actions` array together with `onAction`. Each action has an `id` and a visible `label`, plus an optional `icon`, `description` and `disabled` flag. `onAction` receives the selected action. The menu opens from a **More actions** button, aligned to its end edge.

For a destructive action such as Remove, set `tone: 'danger'` and give it its own `section` so it appears in the danger colour below a divider.

<Canvas of={Stories.Document} />

## Narrow containers

When horizontal space is limited, the actions wrap below the file details so the file information stays readable.

<Canvas of={Stories.NarrowContainer} />

## Status and loading

The `status` text is always visible. Set `loading` while the file details are unavailable to show a row-shaped placeholder with a labelled progress bar.

<Canvas of={Stories.UploadFailed} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Accessibility

- The **Open** and **More actions** buttons include the file name in their accessible names.
- Changes to `status` are announced politely to screen readers.
- Action icons are decorative; each action is named by its label.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './DocumentViewer.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Opens an attached image or document in an accessible full-screen preview."
/>

# DocumentViewer

`DocumentViewer` opens an attached image, PDF or other document in a full-screen preview with zoom, rotation and download controls. Use it to let people read an attachment without leaving the record it belongs to.

## Basic viewer

The viewer is controlled: pass `open` and `onOpenChange`, and render your own trigger, such as the Open button of an `AttachmentRow`. Set `src` to the file URL, `title` to the visible title, and `mediaType` to `image`, `pdf` or `document`.

Each example below starts closed; use its Open button to view the attachment.

<Canvas of={Stories.ImageDocs} />

<Canvas of={Stories.PdfWorkerDocs} />

## Toolbar

The toolbar shows the file name, the current zoom percentage and these actions:

- **Zoom** and **Rotate**, for images, PDF pages and embedded documents.
- **Download**, always available. `downloadName` sets the saved file name.
- **Full screen**, shown only when the browser supports the Fullscreen API.
- **Replace** and **Remove**, shown only when you pass `onReplace` or `onRemove`. Handle any confirmation in your application.

Multi-page PDFs add page navigation in a separate row beneath the toolbar. When you zoom a PDF, the current page stays visible and keeps its scroll position until the sharper version replaces it.

Downloads from another origin need the file host to allow CORS from your application, so the file name can be kept. If a download fails, for example because a presigned URL has expired, the viewer shows an error and stays open; it never navigates away to the file URL.

## PDFs

Images and other documents need no setup. PDFs are rendered page by page with selectable text using the optional `pdfjs-dist` peer dependency. Install a compatible version in your application:

```sh
yarn add pdfjs-dist@^6.2.108
```

PDF.js and its worker are loaded only when a PDF is opened, so they add nothing to your initial bundle. Together they are roughly 635 KiB gzipped.

The viewer fetches each PDF in a single request and makes no later byte-range requests, so a presigned URL only needs to be valid when the document is opened.

### Worker

By default, the viewer locates the PDF.js worker with `new URL('pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.mjs', import.meta.url)`. Vite resolves this in production builds and emits the worker as an asset. For Vite's development server, exclude Breeze UI from dependency pre-bundling:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  optimizeDeps: {
    exclude: ['@motech-development/breeze-ui'],
  },
});
```

With another bundler, or if you prefer not to change `optimizeDeps`, host the worker for your installed `pdfjs-dist` version and pass its URL as `pdfAssets.workerSrc`.

### Fonts and character maps

Some PDFs use predefined Adobe character maps or PDF.js standard fonts. To support them, copy the `cmaps/` and `standard_fonts/` directories from your installed `pdfjs-dist` version to public asset paths, and pass their URLs through `pdfAssets`:

```tsx
<DocumentViewer
  mediaType="pdf"
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  pdfAssets={{
    cMapUrl: '/pdfjs/cmaps',
    standardFontDataUrl: '/pdfjs/standard_fonts',
  }}
  src={source}
  title="Quarterly report"
/>
```

The files must come from the same `pdfjs-dist` version. A trailing slash is added to each URL. Documents that do not use these assets work without them.

### Without PDF.js

If PDF.js is not installed or cannot render a file, the viewer shows the PDF in the browser's built-in PDF viewer instead. It fetches the file first, so the source must be same-origin or allow CORS. If the fetch fails, the viewer reports that the preview is unavailable and Download remains available.

When `pdfjs-dist` is not installed, Vite builds still succeed and use this fallback. Other bundlers may fail the build; install `pdfjs-dist`, or configure the bundler to ignore the missing optional module.

## Opening from an AttachmentRow

Give the `AttachmentRow` and the viewer the same unique `transitionName` to animate between the row and the viewer in both directions. The file is revealed once the opening animation finishes. Closing returns to the row, and any sheet or dialog around it stays open. Browsers without view transition support, and people who prefer reduced motion, see the same flow without animation.

<Canvas of={Stories.FromAttachmentRowDocs} />

## Accessibility

- `title` names the viewer.
- The viewer is non-modal. The page or sheet beneath it stays open and interactive, and remains available to assistive technology.
- While the viewer is open, Tab and Shift+Tab keep focus within its controls, and page scrolling is locked.
- Escape and the Close button close the viewer.
- Opened from a sheet, the viewer covers the screen while the sheet stays open behind it. Closing the viewer returns focus to the sheet, and closing the sheet also closes the viewer.

Rendered PDF pages are drawn as images, so screen readers cannot read their content. PDF text can be selected, but document tags, reading order and text in scanned images are not available. The viewer shows a notice to this effect and offers the original file for download, so make sure the surrounding record describes the attachment.

For `mediaType="document"`, the browser's own viewer displays the file, and its controls, keyboard support and accessibility vary by browser and file type. These frames are sandboxed, so embedded HTML or SVG cannot run scripts in your application.

## API

<ArgTypes of={Stories.PdfWorker} />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './FileDropZone.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Accepts files by drag and drop or through an accessible picker button, with visible validation feedback."
/>

# FileDropZone

`FileDropZone` lets people add files by dragging them onto the drop area or by using the **Choose files** button. `label` is shown above the drop area and names it.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Compact

Set `compact` to show the drop area as a single row, the same height as an `AttachmentRow`. A single attachment then keeps its position whether or not a file is attached. The secondary text stays on one line and is truncated with an ellipsis.

<Canvas of={Stories.Compact} />

## Take photo

Set `camera` to add a **Take photo** button before **Choose files**. On phones it requests the rear camera, although the browser or device may use its own default; on other devices it opens an image picker.

Cameras produce JPEG photos, so **Take photo** appears only when `accept` is omitted or allows JPEG through `image/*`, `image/jpeg`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `*/*`. Photos go through the same type, size and count checks as chosen files and are passed to `onFilesAdded` in the same way.

On touch devices and narrow screens (below 901px), **Take photo** is filled in the brand colour. On narrow screens:

- in the default layout, **Take photo** fills the action row and the drag-and-drop instruction is hidden;
- in `compact` mode, both buttons show only their icons and keep their accessible names.

<Canvas of={Stories.TakePhoto} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Phone} />

<Canvas of={Stories.CompactPhone} />

## File limits

- `accept` takes a comma-separated list of file extensions and MIME types, such as `.pdf,image/*`. Dropped files are checked against the same list. `.jpg` and `.jpeg` each accept either extension, and an untyped file named `.jpg` or `.jpeg` is treated as `image/jpeg`.
- `maxSize` sets the largest file size, in bytes.
- `maxFiles` sets the total number of attachments allowed. When files are already attached, pass their number as `currentFileCount`.

Accepted files are passed to `onFilesAdded` as a read-only array. Uploading and storing them is up to your application. Rejected files show their reason as visible text.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithExistingFiles} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ChooseAFile} />

## Localisation

The button text, instructions and feedback can be translated through the `messages` prop of `BreezeProvider`. Keep the placeholders listed in the BreezeProvider locale section. Each message is announced in its own language.

## Accessibility

- **Choose files** opens the native file picker, so keyboard users can add files without dragging.
- Each rejection reason is also announced through a polite live region.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

/>

# StatStrip

`StatStrip` shows a few headline currency figures, such as a balance and the VAT owed, as labelled cells in one panel.

<Canvas of={Stories.Overview} />

## Figures

Pass your data as `items`, and use `getItem` to return a `StatStripItemDescriptor` for each one:

- `id`: a stable identifier;
- `label`: the visible name of the figure;
- `value` and `currency`: the amount and its ISO 4217 currency code;
- `badge` (optional): a badge after the label showing the figure's scope, such as the VAT scheme. It accepts `children`, `variant` and `aria-label`.

Amounts are formatted as currency for the provider locale, with a minus sign for negative amounts. A non-finite `value` or a malformed currency code, one that is not three letters, throws a `RangeError`. Codes are not checked against ISO 4217, so an unknown well-formed code is displayed as written. If you need to limit the currencies shown, validate the codes before passing them in.

## Loading

Set `loading` to show three placeholder cells shaped like labels and figures. `items` and `getItem` are optional while loading.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Phone layout

Below 901px, the cells stack in a single column with a divider between them.

<Canvas of={Stories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

The panel is a group named by the required `aria-label`. Its figures form a description list, so screen readers announce each label with its amount.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './StatePanel.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Presents an empty or error state as a labelled section with one optional action."
/>

# StatePanel

`StatePanel` explains why there is no content to show, either because there is nothing yet or because loading it failed. Pass a `title`, a `description` and a `variant` of `empty` or `error`, with an optional action.

## Empty states

Use `variant="empty"` when there is no content yet. Add an `action`, such as creating the first item, when there is an obvious next step.

<Canvas of={Stories.Empty} />

<Canvas of={Stories.EmptyWithAction} />

If the panel shows the page's primary action, leave that action out of the page header so it does not appear twice.

## Error states

Use `variant="error"` when content could not be loaded. To let people retry, pass an `action` whose `onAction` performs the recovery.

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ErrorWithRecovery} />

## Icon

Empty states show a document icon in the brand colour, and error states a warning icon in the danger colour. Set `icon` to another Breeze icon when it better describes the content.

<Canvas of={Stories.CustomIcon} />

## Accessibility

The panel is a section labelled by its title. It is not a live region, so when it replaces content dynamically, announce the change yourself if people need to hear it.

## API

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Empty} />

actions-button--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Button.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Performs an action or submits a form." />

# Button

Buttons let people perform an action, such as saving a record or submitting a form.

## Basic button

`Button` has four variants: `primary` (default), `secondary`, `quiet` and `danger`. `children` sets the visible label.

<Canvas of={Stories.Primary} />

## Secondary button

Secondary buttons are neutral alternatives to the primary action, such as cancelling.

<Canvas of={Stories.Secondary} />

## Quiet button

Quiet buttons are text-only actions with no border or fill, for actions that sit alongside content, such as **Mark all as read** in a panel header or **Download** on a row. They come in one size and do not accept `size`. Use a `Link` instead when the action navigates.

<Canvas of={Stories.Quiet} />

<Canvas of={Stories.RowAction} />

## Danger button

Danger buttons are destructive actions. Use a label that states what will be removed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Danger} />

## Sizes

`size` accepts `sm`, `md` (default) and `lg`, with minimum heights of 32, 36 and 52px. Small labels are 12px and the others 13px, all semibold. Sizes apply to the `primary`, `secondary` and `danger` variants.

<Canvas of={Stories.TreatmentsAndSizes} />

Labels wrap and increase the height of the button:

<Canvas of={Stories.LongLabel} />

## Icon

Set `icon` to show a Breeze icon before the label. It works with every variant and size, and is 15px at `size="sm"` and 16px at `md` and `lg`. While loading, the icon is hidden along with the label.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithIcon} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while the action is in progress. A placeholder replaces the label, and the button cannot be activated again until loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Disabled

`disabled` prevents activation and removes the button from the tab order.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Handling actions

`onAction` is called with no arguments when the button is activated by pointer, touch or keyboard.

<Canvas of={Stories.Activation} />

## Form submission

Buttons default to `type="button"`. Set `type="submit"` to submit the surrounding form, and handle submission on the form. `form`, `name` and `value` are also supported.

## Accessibility

- The label is the button's accessible name, including while it is loading. Icons are decorative.
- On touch devices, buttons have a minimum 44px target. Quiet buttons have a minimum 44px height on touch devices and below 901px.
- `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup` are supported.

## API

<ArgTypes />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Calendar.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A six-week, Monday-first calendar with ISO date values."
/>

# Calendar

`Calendar` shows a month grid for picking a single date. To pick a date from a form field, use `DatePicker`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

The header shows the month with previous and next month buttons. Weeks start on Monday, and each month shows six rows, with dates from the neighbouring months in muted text. Weekday names use the provider locale. The selected date has a brand fill, and today has a brand outline unless it is selected.

## Disabled

Set `disabled` to prevent the date from being changed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Controlled values

Pass `value` and `onChange` to control the selected date. `onChange` receives an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string.

For an uncontrolled calendar, use `defaultValue` with an optional `onChange`. Controlled and uncontrolled props cannot be combined.

## Accessibility

- `label` names the calendar.
- Use the arrow keys to move between dates and Enter or Space to select one.
- Each date is announced with its full weekday and date name in the provider locale.
- The selected date's fill has at least 3:1 contrast with the background in both light and dark appearances.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Card.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Decorates related content as a bordered Breeze panel."
/>

# Card

`Card` groups related content on a bordered panel. Set `padding` to a value from the Breeze spacing scale; it defaults to `4`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Surface} />

## Raised cards

Use `variant="raised"` for a group nested inside another surface. It does not add stronger elevation.

<Canvas of={Stories.Raised} />

## Titles

Set `title` to add a header with a second-level heading. Add `count` to show a neutral count beside the title.

<Canvas of={Stories.TitledWithCount} />

Use `action` for one control at the end of the header, such as a link to the full list. With a title, `padding` applies only to the content below it, so set `padding={0}` for rows that run edge to edge.

<Canvas of={Stories.TitledWithAction} />

## Loading

Cards have no loading state of their own. Use loading-capable children or `Skeleton` elements inside the card so the placeholders match the final content.

## Accessibility

- The card itself is not interactive and cannot be made clickable as a whole.
- Set `element` to `article`, `aside` or `section` only when that grouping is meaningful, and give a region a name with `title` or `aria-label`.
- A titled card is named by its heading, so `aria-label` is not accepted alongside `title`.

## API

<ArgTypes />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Checkbox.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A flat labelled checkbox with semantic boolean changes."
/>

# Checkbox

`Checkbox` lets people turn a single option on or off. Pass the visible text as `label`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Description and errors

Use `description` for guidance shown under the label. Set `error` to a non-empty message to show it in the same place and mark the checkbox invalid.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

## Required

Set `required` to mark the checkbox as required.

<Canvas of={Stories.Required} />

## Disabled

Set `disabled` to prevent selection and focus. The box is greyed out and the label stays legible.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Read only

Set `readOnly` to prevent changes while keeping the checkbox focusable and included in form submission.

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while the value is unavailable. The checkbox keeps its shape, announces the provider's loading message and cannot be selected until loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled values

Pass `selected` and `onChange` to control the checkbox. `onChange` receives the new `boolean` value.

For an uncontrolled checkbox, use `defaultSelected` with an optional `onChange`. Controlled and uncontrolled props cannot be combined.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Blur

`onBlur` reports that focus has left the checkbox, for example to show a
validation error only once the user has moved on. Like `onChange`, it receives
no DOM event.

<Canvas of={Stories.Blur} />

## Accessibility

- The checkbox is a native input named by its `label`. Clicking the description also toggles it, but the description is not part of the name.
- The description and error are announced with the checkbox.
- `ref` gives access to the native input.

## API

<Meta of={Stories} summary="An independently selectable pill-shaped filter." />

# Chip

`Chip` is a compact, pill-shaped toggle for filtering content. Each chip is turned on and off independently, even in a row with other chips.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Pressed state

Use `defaultPressed` for an uncontrolled chip, or `pressed` and `onChange` to control it. `onChange` receives the new pressed value. Use only one of these approaches for each chip.

<Canvas of={Stories.Pressed} />

<Canvas of={Stories.FilterRow} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while a choice is being saved. A placeholder replaces the visible label, and the chip keeps its name and width. It can be activated again once loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Disabled

Set `disabled` to prevent activation.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Accessibility

- The chip is a button named by its visible label. Use `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to give it an alternative name, and `aria-describedby` to add a description.
- Its state is announced as pressed or not pressed, and it can be toggled with the keyboard.
- Chips are at least 34px tall and have a minimum 44px touch target.

forms-combobox--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './ComboBox.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A filterable suggestion field with optional free text."
/>

# ComboBox

`ComboBox` is a text field with a list of suggestions that filters as people type. Use it when there are too many options to scan in a select, or when people may enter their own value.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Items

Pass your data as `items`, and use `getItem` to return an `ItemDescriptor` for each one. It has an `id` and a `label`, plus an optional `description`, `icon`, `badge` and `disabled` flag. Items are rendered from these fields only.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

## Filtering and free text

Typing filters the suggestions by their labels. Set `allowsCustomValue` to also accept text that does not match a suggestion; `onChange` then receives the selected item, the entered text or `null`.

When nothing matches, or `items` is empty, the list stays open with a message that repeats the entered text. With `allowsCustomValue`, the list closes instead, because the entered text is already a valid value.

<Canvas of={Stories.NoMatches} />

<Canvas of={Stories.FreeText} />

## Validation

Set `error` to a non-empty message to show it and mark the field invalid. Set `required` to mark the field as required.

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

## Read only and disabled

Set `readOnly` to show a value that cannot be changed, or `disabled` to prevent interaction.

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while the value is unavailable. The field keeps its shape and cannot be used until loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled values

Pass `value` and `onChange` to control the field. `onChange` receives the selected item, custom text or `null`.

For an uncontrolled field, use `defaultValue` with an optional `onChange`. Controlled and uncontrolled props cannot be combined.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Blur

`onBlur` reports that focus has left the field, for example to show a
validation error only once the user has moved on. Like `onChange`, it receives
no DOM event. It reports once when focus leaves the whole field: using the
suggestions button and choosing a suggestion do not count.

<Canvas of={Stories.Blur} />

## Accessibility

- The visible label names the input, and its description and error are announced with it.
- Use the arrow keys to move through the suggestions, Enter to choose one and Escape to close the list.

## API

forms-datepicker--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './DatePicker.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A date field, required by default, with an ISO value and localized trigger."
/>

# DatePicker

`DatePicker` is a form field for choosing a date from a calendar. The field shows the selected date in the provider locale's long format, and opens the calendar when activated. Values are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` strings.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

When no date is selected, the field shows `placeholder`, or the provider's `selectDate` message if you omit it.

## Today

The calendar has a **Today** button that selects the current date, reports it through `onChange` and closes the calendar.

<Canvas of={Stories.TodayAction} />

## Validation

Set `error` to a non-empty message to show it and mark the field invalid.

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

## Disabled

Set `disabled` to prevent interaction. A disabled date is not included in form submission.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Read only

Set `readOnly` to show a recorded date that cannot be changed, for example in a view mode. The field stays focusable and the date is included in form submission, but the calendar does not open.

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

## Optional dates

Unlike other fields, `DatePicker` is required by default, and a required date cannot be cleared.

Set `required={false}` to make the date optional. The calendar then shows a clear button beside **Today**, which empties the field, closes the calendar and reports `null`. The clear button is unavailable while the field is empty.

With an optional date, `onChange` must accept `null`, and an uncontrolled field can start from `defaultValue={null}`. On a required date, `onChange` only ever receives a date string, and TypeScript rejects `defaultValue={null}`. A controlled required field can still pass `value={null}` until a date is chosen.

<Canvas of={Stories.Optional} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while the date is unavailable. The label, field and supporting text are replaced by placeholders, the provider's loading message is announced, and the field cannot be used or submitted until loading ends. Errors are hidden and an open calendar closes; the selected value is kept.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled values

Pass `value` and `onChange` to control the field. Set `value` to `null` for an empty field.

For an uncontrolled field, use `defaultValue` with an optional `onChange`. Controlled and uncontrolled props cannot be combined. An uncontrolled field returns to `defaultValue` when its form is reset.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Blur

`onBlur` reports that focus has left the field, for example to show a
validation error only once the user has moved on. Like `onChange`, it receives
no DOM event. It reports once when focus leaves the whole field: moving into
the calendar and choosing a date do not count.

<Canvas of={Stories.Blur} />

## Forms

Set `name` to include the date in form submission as an ISO string; an empty field submits an empty string. There is no `autoComplete` prop, as browser autofill does not apply to the date button.

## Localisation

Override the provider's `selectDate`, `today`, `clearDate` and `required` messages to translate the placeholder, the **Today** and clear buttons, and the required announcement. Untranslated messages are in English and marked as `en-GB` for screen readers.

## Accessibility

- The visible label names the field, which announces whether it is required or invalid.
- The calendar supports keyboard navigation and announces dates in the provider locale.
- On touch devices, controls have a minimum 44px target.

## API

<ArgTypes />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Dialog.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Opens a modal surface for a focused task." />

# Dialog

`Dialog` opens a centred modal window for a focused task that takes priority over the rest of the page. Render it inside `BreezeProvider`.

## Basic dialog

`trigger` sets the label of the button that opens the dialog. `title` sets the dialog's visible heading and accessible name, and `children` its content. The dialog also includes a close button.

```tsx
<Dialog title="Delivery details" trigger="View delivery details">
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Dialog>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Controlled

By default, the dialog manages its own open state. Set `defaultOpen` to start it open, and use `onOpenChange` to respond to changes.

To control the dialog from your application state, pass both `open` and `onOpenChange`. `open` and `defaultOpen` cannot be combined.

```tsx
<Dialog
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  title="Delivery details"
  trigger="View delivery details"
>
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Dialog>
```

## Dismissal

By default, pressing Escape or clicking outside the dialog closes it. Set `dismissible={false}` to keep it open in those cases; the close button still works.

## Accessibility

- Focus moves into the dialog when it opens, stays inside it while open, and is restored when it closes.
- The close button's accessible name comes from the provider's messages.
- The dialog keeps the provider's locale and text direction.
- Opening and closing animations respect the reduced-motion preference.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Drawer.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Opens a modal surface from the edge of the page." />

# Drawer

A drawer is a modal panel that slides in from the edge of the page. Use it for a focused task, such as recording a transaction, or for supporting content that should not replace the current page.

## Basic drawer

Pass `trigger` as the label of the button that opens the drawer, `title` as its heading and `children` as its content. The drawer includes a close button, labelled with the provider's messages.

```tsx
<Drawer title="Delivery details" trigger="View delivery details">
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Drawer>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Content and footer

The content scrolls independently between the heading and the footer. The footer stays pinned to the bottom and appears only when you pass at least one of these props:

- `footerStart` places an action at the start, such as Delete on an edit form.
- `footerSummary` shows a short muted line that takes the free width and truncates.
- `footerActions` places the actions at the end, such as Cancel and Save.

```tsx
<Drawer
  footerActions={
    <>
      <Button onAction={close} variant="secondary">
        Cancel
      </Button>
      <Button onAction={save}>Save transaction</Button>
    </>
  }
  footerSummary="Takes £139.00 off the balance now"
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  title="New transaction"
  trigger="Record transaction"
>
  <TextField label="Name" />
</Drawer>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.RecordTransaction} />

When the footer runs out of room, the actions wrap onto their own line and stay at the end. Below 768px, the summary keeps its full text and the actions move to the next line; the summary truncates only when it is wider than the footer.

<Canvas of={Stories.EditTransaction} />

Below the `md` breakpoint, the drawer fills the screen and slides up from the bottom.

## Open state

By default, the drawer manages its own open state. Set `defaultOpen` to start open, and use `onOpenChange` to respond to changes.

To control the drawer from your own state, pass both `open` and `onOpenChange`. `open` and `defaultOpen` cannot be combined.

```tsx
<Drawer
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  title="Delivery details"
  trigger="View delivery details"
>
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Drawer>
```

## Dismissal

By default, pressing Escape or clicking outside the drawer closes it. Set `dismissible={false}` to keep it open in those cases, for example while a form has unsaved changes. The close button still works.

## Opening other overlays from a drawer

A `Popover` opened inside a drawer appears above it. The drawer stays interactive and keeps its dimmed backdrop, and Escape closes the popover before the drawer.

A `DocumentViewer` opened inside a drawer covers it with a full-screen view. The drawer stays open underneath, keeping its state, and remains available to screen readers. Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the full-screen view, and Escape closes it before the drawer, returning focus to the button that opened it.

See the `Foundations/Overlay stack` stories for more combinations.

## Accessibility

Opening the drawer moves focus into it, and focus stays inside while it is open. Closing it returns focus to the trigger. The drawer's DOM is rendered in a portal, but it stays in your React tree and keeps the provider's locale and text direction.

The open and close animations respect the user's reduced-motion setting. As soon as a drawer starts to close, the content beneath it becomes interactive again, without waiting for the animation to finish.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Grid.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Arranges content in equal or main-and-aside responsive columns."
/>

# Grid

`Grid` arranges content in one, two or three equal columns, or in a main column beside an aside. Set `columns` to choose the layout (it defaults to `2`) and `gap` to choose the spacing from the Breeze spacing scale.

By default, a multi-column grid collapses to a single column below the `md` breakpoint. Use `collapseBelow` to change the breakpoint.

<Canvas of={Stories.Responsive} />

## Fixed columns

Set `collapseBelow="none"` to keep the columns at every width. Use this only for content that still reads well on narrow screens.

<Canvas of={Stories.Fixed} />

## Main and aside

Set `columns="mainAside"` for a page with a primary column and a supporting aside, such as a dashboard overview. Pass exactly two children: the main content first, then the aside.

The aside is 300px wide and the main column fills the remaining space. Each column keeps its own height, so a short aside does not stretch to match the main column. Below `md`, the aside stacks under the main content; `collapseBelow` changes this breakpoint as it does for equal columns.

<Canvas of={Stories.MainAside} />

## Loading

`Grid` has no loading state of its own. Show loading inside each item, using components with a `loading` prop or a `Skeleton` sized like the final content.

## Accessibility

`Grid` changes the visual layout, not the reading order. Write children in the order they should be read.

# Icon

`Icon` displays an icon from the Breeze icon set. Set `name` to choose the icon; names describe what the icon means, such as `incoming` or `document`, rather than what it looks like.

<Canvas of={Stories.Gallery} />

## Sizes

Set `size` to choose one of the following square sizes. It defaults to `sm`.

| Size  | Pixels | Typical use                                                 |
| ----- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `2xs` | 14     | Overlay close and menu trigger chevrons                     |
| `xs`  | 15     | Field chevrons, selected ticks, row tiles and small buttons |
| `sm`  | 16     | Buttons, menu items, calendar navigation and toasts         |
| `md`  | 17     | Date picker trigger and compact upload thumbnail            |
| `lg`  | 20     | Medium icon buttons                                         |
| `xl`  | 21     | Bottom navigation                                           |
| `2xl` | 22     | Large icon tiles in content states                          |
| `3xl` | 24     | Large icon buttons, such as the raised action               |
| `4xl` | 26     | Stacked file drop zone                                      |

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

## Accessible names

Icons are decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology. Pass `label` only when the icon carries meaning that no nearby text provides; screen readers then announce the label.

<Canvas of={Stories.Named} />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './IconButton.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Performs an action from an icon alone." />

# IconButton

An icon button performs an action using an icon alone, such as closing a panel or opening more actions. Use it when the icon is clear enough without visible text.

## Basic icon button

Set `name` to choose an icon from the Breeze icon set, and `label` to name the action for screen readers. `label` is required because the button has no visible text.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Variants and sizes

`variant` accepts the same values as `Button`: `secondary` (default), `primary`, `quiet` and `danger`. `secondary` suits most icon-only actions, such as Close and More actions, which sit beside content rather than leading it.

`size` accepts `sm`, `md` (default) and `lg`. The button is a 32, 36 or 52px square, with a 16, 20 or 24px icon.

<Canvas of={Stories.TreatmentsAndSizes} />

## Shapes

`shape` accepts `square` (default), with rounded corners, and `circle`, for a standalone action such as the centre action in `ApplicationShell`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Shapes} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while the action is in progress. The icon is replaced by a placeholder, and the button cannot be activated again until loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Disabled

Set `disabled` to prevent activation. A disabled button is also removed from the tab order.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Handling actions

Pass `onAction` to respond when the button is activated by click, tap or keyboard. It is called with no arguments.

<Canvas of={Stories.Activation} />

## Accessibility

Screen readers announce the `label` as the button's name, including while it is loading; the icon itself is hidden. On touch devices the button has a target of at least 44px.

The button also accepts `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup` when it opens or controls other content.

## API

<ArgTypes />

# IconTile

`IconTile` shows an icon on a soft coloured background. Use it to illustrate empty states, list rows and similar content. Set `name` to choose the icon and `tone` to choose the colour; `tone` defaults to `brand`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Treatments} />

## Direction markers

For a money-in or money-out marker, use the small circular tile with `shape="circle"` and `size="sm"`. Use `tone="positive"` for money in and `tone="strong"` for money out. `strong` has the same background as `neutral`, with a darker icon.

<Canvas of={Stories.Direction} />

## Accessibility

The icon is decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology. Pass `label` only when no nearby text describes what it means. Do not rely on the tile colour alone to convey meaning.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Inline.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Arranges children horizontally on the Breeze spacing scale."
/>

# Inline

`Inline` arranges related items in a row, such as a group of buttons or badges. Set `gap` to choose the spacing from the Breeze spacing scale, `verticalAlign` to align items (centred by default) and `justify` to distribute them along the row.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Wrapping

Set `wrap` when the items may not fit on one line, such as a list of labels or actions. Items that do not fit move onto the next row.

<Canvas of={Stories.Wrapped} />

## Loading

`Inline` has no loading state of its own. Show loading inside each item, using components with a `loading` prop or a `Skeleton` sized like the final content.

## Accessibility

`Inline` renders a `div` by default, which adds no meaning for assistive technology. Use `element` to choose a landmark or region only when the content is one, and name it with `aria-label`. Items are read in the same order they appear.

## API

navigation-link--docs.content: import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import * as Stories from './Link.stories'; # Link `Link` is a standalone text link without an underline, such as a View all link in a panel header. It renders a native anchor, so `href` works as usual: keyboard access, opening in a new tab and copying the address all behave as people expect. For an action that does not navigate, use a quiet `Button` instead. Without a router, the link uses the browser's normal navigation. With a router configured on `BreezeProvider`, same-origin links navigate through the router instead. ## Router navigation Pass a `router` to `BreezeProvider` when links should change the page without a full reload. `Link` sends the destination and its optional `transitionTypes` to the router, which decides whether to use a browser view transition; see Motion. ```tsx Transactions ``` The link calls `router.navigate(path, { transitionTypes })`. `transitionTypes` defaults to an empty list, so an existing `navigate(href)` function that takes one argument works unchanged. The router receives the path the browser would navigate to, not the raw `href`: a root-relative path including any query string. Relative values such as `accounts`, `../reports` or `?page=2` are resolved against the current page first, so on `/accounts/transactions/`, `href="?page=2"` navigates to `/accounts/transactions/?page=2`. The path already includes any base path your application is served under. **If your router adds its own `basename`, remove the base from the path before navigating**, or it will appear twice. ### When the browser navigates instead The router handles only a plain primary click on a same-origin HTTP or HTTPS link. The browser navigates as normal for external links, downloads, links with a `target` other than `_self`, links containing a `#` fragment, and clicks with a modifier key, such as Ctrl or Cmd to open a new tab. ## Variants The default link uses the brand text colour. Set `variant="subtle"` for a lower-emphasis link. ## Accessibility A `Link` is distinguished from text by colour alone, so place it on its own rather than inside a sentence. On touch devices and below the `md` breakpoint, it has a minimum height of 44px. Screen readers announce the link's text as its name. Use `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when the text does not describe the destination, and `aria-current` when the link points to the current page. ## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Menu.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="A compact list of actions opened from a button." />

# Menu

A menu shows a list of actions when someone presses its button. Use it for
secondary actions, such as account settings, that should stay out of the way
until needed.

## Basic menu

Pass `trigger` as the button's visible label, your data as `items`, and a
`getItem` function that describes each item. `onAction` is called with the
selected item from `items`, as it is in `Select`, `ComboBox` and `ToggleGroup`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

When several buttons on a page share the same visible label, set
`triggerAriaLabel` to give each one a distinct name for screen readers while
keeping the visible label short.

## Item content

`getItem` returns a `MenuItemDescriptor` for each item:

- `id` and `label` are required. Each `id` must be unique within the menu.
- `description`, `icon` or `initials`, `badge`, `disabled`, `section` and
  `tone` are optional.

Keep labels concise. Use a description for a short explanation, and icons when
they help people scan the choices.

When any item has an icon or initials, every label lines up: items without
either keep the space empty, and in a menu with initials, icons are centred in
the tile's width. In a menu with neither, labels start at the edge.

## Icon-only trigger

For a compact button such as More actions, omit `trigger` and set `triggerIcon`
and `triggerAriaLabel`. `triggerAriaLabel` is required here, because it is the
button's only name.

<Canvas of={Stories.IconOnlyTrigger} />

## Sections

Give items a `section` to group them. Items that share a section `id` appear
together, where the first of them appears in `items`, with dividers between
sections. A section `label` is shown as a header and names the group for screen
readers. Without a label, the items are separated by dividers only.

Set `initials` instead of `icon` to show a short code, such as a company's
initials, in a tile before the label. The tile is decorative, so the label must
still identify the item.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sections} />

## Destructive actions

Set `tone: 'danger'` on an action that removes or discards something, such as
Remove, to show it in the danger colour. Place it last, in its own `section`,
so a divider separates it from the other actions.

The action runs as soon as it is selected, like any other. If it needs
confirming, or its result needs showing, do that in the page or a dialog.

<Canvas of={Stories.DestructiveAction} />

## Width

The open menu fits its items and is never narrower than its button. `width`
sets its minimum width:

- `md` (default) is 256px and suits a list of names, such as a company switcher.
- `sm` is 208px and suits a short list of actions, such as the file actions in
  `AttachmentRow`.

<Canvas of={Stories.NarrowWidth} />

## Placement

The menu opens below its button with their start edges aligned. Set
`placement="bottom end"` to align their end edges instead, for a button at the
end of a row. Start and end follow the provider's text direction, and the menu
moves if needed to fit on screen.

## Loading

Set `loading` while the menu is not ready to open. The button shows a loading
bar and keeps its size and accessible name; an icon-only button replaces its
icon with a placeholder, as `IconButton` does. Actions in a menu that is
already open remain available.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled open state

The menu closes when an action is selected. Show the action's progress,
confirmation or errors in the page or dialog that follows.

By default, the menu manages whether it is open; set `defaultOpen` to start
open. To control it from your own state, pass both `open` and `onOpenChange`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## When to use a popover instead

A menu can contain only actions, optionally grouped into sections. Use a
`Popover` instead for a panel that also shows information, places controls
inside a row or header, or includes a toggle group. Screen readers present a
menu as its actions alone, so plain text is skipped, and the arrow keys cannot
reach a button placed inside an item or header.

For example, an account panel that lists notifications with a Download action,
offers Mark all as read and an `AppearanceControl`, and links to settings
should be a `Popover`.

## Accessibility

- Open the menu by pressing its button, or with Enter, Space or ArrowDown when
  the button has focus.
- Use the arrow keys to move between enabled actions, or type the start of a
  label to jump to it.
- Enter or Space selects the focused action.
- Escape closes the menu and returns focus to its button.

## API

<ArgTypes />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './NumberField.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Locale-aware numeric entry with semantic number changes."
/>

# NumberField

`NumberField` is a labelled input for entering numbers, such as an amount.
It reads and displays numbers using the provider's locale, and shows figures
with tabular numerals so digits line up.

There are no stepper buttons. Up and Down arrow keys change the value by
`step`, which defaults to `1`. Beyond the locale's number conventions, values
are not formatted unless you pass `formatOptions`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Sizes

`size` defaults to `md`, a 38px control with 13px figures. Use `lg` for a
form's main amount: a 52px control with 20px semibold figures. Fields in the
same row should use the same size.

<Canvas of={Stories.Large} />

## Description and errors

Use `description` for guidance about what to enter. Pass a non-empty `error`
to mark the field invalid and show the message; there is no separate `invalid`
prop.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

## States

`required`, `disabled` and `readOnly` behave as they do on a native input.

Set `loading` while the value is not yet available. The field keeps its shape,
screen readers announce the provider's loading message, and the value cannot be
typed or stepped until loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Required} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

<Canvas of={Stories.LargeLoading} />

## Controlled

To control the value, pass both `value` and `onChange`. `onChange` receives the
new number, not a DOM event. While the input is empty, the value is `NaN`, so
you can tell an empty field from zero.

For an uncontrolled field, pass `defaultValue` and optionally `onChange`.
Controlled and uncontrolled props cannot be combined.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Blur

`onBlur` reports that focus has left the field, for example to show a
validation error only once the user has moved on. Like `onChange`, it receives
no DOM event. The typed number is committed through `onChange` before `onBlur`
reports.

<Canvas of={Stories.Blur} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the input, and screen readers announce the description
and any error with it. Use `ref` to reach the native input, for example to
focus it.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Popover.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Opens contextual content beside its trigger." />

# Popover

A popover shows contextual content next to the button that opens it. It is not modal: the rest of the page stays usable, and the page is not dimmed behind it.

Use `Popover` rather than `Menu` when the content mixes information with controls, such as a list of notifications with their own actions beside an `AppearanceControl`. A `Menu` holds only a list of actions.

## Basic popover

Pass `trigger` as the label of the button that opens the popover, `title` as its heading and `children` as its content. The popover includes a close button, labelled with the provider's messages.

```tsx
<Popover title="Delivery details" trigger="View delivery details">
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Popover>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Open state

By default, the popover manages its own open state. Set `defaultOpen` to start open, and use `onOpenChange` to respond to changes.

To control the popover from your own state, pass both `open` and `onOpenChange`. `open` and `defaultOpen` cannot be combined.

```tsx
<Popover
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  title="Delivery details"
  trigger="View delivery details"
>
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Popover>
```

## Dismissal

By default, pressing Escape or clicking outside the popover closes it. Set `dismissible={false}` to keep it open in those cases; the close button still works. A popover with `variant="panel"` has no close button, so it is always dismissible.

## Placement

`placement` accepts `top`, `bottom` (default), `start`, `end` or `bottom end`. Use `bottom end` to open below the button with their end edges aligned, for a button at the end of a bar. Start and end follow the provider's text direction, and the popover moves if needed to fit on screen.

## Panels

Set `variant="panel"` for content that makes its own purpose clear, such as an account panel of notifications and settings. A panel has no visible title or close button, but `title` still names it for screen readers.

A panel's content runs edge to edge with no padding. The panel is at least 336px wide and grows to fit its content; on narrow screens it spans the viewport, less 12px on each side. It closes with Escape or a click outside it.

### Initials and unread indicator

Set `triggerInitials` to open the popover from a circular button showing a person's initials. `trigger` then becomes the button's accessible name only, so describe what it opens.

Set `triggerIndicator` to add a dot to the button, for example for unread notifications. Screen readers announce the provider's unread-items message rather than the dot itself. If you know the count, include it in `trigger`, for example "Account and notifications, 2 unread".

```tsx
<Popover
  placement="bottom end"
  title="Account and notifications"
  trigger="Account and notifications, 2 unread"
  triggerIndicator
  triggerInitials="MG"
  variant="panel"
>
  {/* Notifications, AppearanceControl and account links */}
</Popover>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.AccountPanel} />

## Inside a drawer

A popover opened inside a `Drawer` appears above it, and the drawer stays interactive and keeps its dimmed backdrop. Escape closes the popover first and returns focus to its button; pressing Escape again closes the drawer. See the `Foundations/Overlay stack` stories for examples.

## Accessibility

Opening the popover moves focus into it, and closing it returns focus to the button. Focus is not trapped, so people can Tab out of the popover to the rest of the page. The popover's DOM is rendered in a portal, but it stays in your React tree and keeps the provider's locale and text direction.

The open and close animations respect the user's reduced-motion setting. As soon as a popover starts to close, the content beneath it becomes interactive again, without waiting for the animation to finish.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './RowList.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A keyboard-accessible list of aligned, actionable rows."
/>

# RowList

`RowList` displays data as a list of rows that people can act on, such as
transactions or documents. Each row has a leading label, optional metadata and
a trailing value, aligned in columns across the list. The list has no column
headers.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Row content

Pass your data as `items` and a `getItem` function that returns a
`RowListItemDescriptor` for each item:

- `id` and `label` are required. Keep each `id` unique and stable, so the
  focused row stays in place when the data changes.
- `description`, `icon`, `badge` and `disabled` are optional.
- `metadata` takes text or an ISO calendar date.
- `value` takes text or a currency amount, formatted in the provider's locale.
  A currency `value` is formatted by `Typography`, so a non-finite amount or a
  malformed currency code throws a `RangeError` when the row is displayed.
- `metadataAmount` adds a second, muted currency column, such as VAT, between
  the metadata and the value. It is formatted like a currency `value`, without
  `tone`.

A metadata or value column takes up space only when at least one row in the
list uses it; otherwise the label extends into that space.

## Sections

Give rows a `section` object to group them under section headers. Keep each
section `id` stable when rows are added or merged.

Set the section's optional `summary` to show content at the end of its header.
The summary is read from the first row in each section:

- A currency summary takes the same fields as a currency `value`, shown at the
  header's 12px size, plus a `label` that screen readers announce before the
  amount, such as “Confirmed daily total”. The list does not add up the amounts
  for you; pass the total with its `tone` and `sign`.
- A text summary shows a muted note instead, such as “Not in the balance yet”
  for a section without a total.

<Canvas of={Stories.Money} />

## Money in and out

Currency values use the compact `amount` role from `Typography`, in the
default text colour. For money in, set `tone: 'positive'` and `sign: 'always'`
to show an explicit `+`; negative amounts use a true minus sign. `sign` works as
it does in `Typography`.

Set a row's `direction` to `in` or `out` to colour its icon tile for money in
or out, and pair it with the `incoming` or `outgoing` icon. Without
`direction`, the tile is neutral. Colour is never the only signal: the sign and
icon also show the direction.

<Canvas of={Stories.Activity} />

## Phone layout

Below the `md` breakpoint, the value stays at the end of the row, the metadata
columns are hidden, and a row's badge moves under its description so the label
keeps the full width. Keep anything essential in the label, description or
value.

<Canvas of={Stories.Phone} />

## Row actions

Each row is an action, not a selection: the list keeps no selection state.
Activating a row calls `onAction` with that row's item from `items`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Merging} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while fetching the first page of data or refreshing it:

- An empty list shows three placeholder rows, and screen readers hear a single
  loading announcement.
- A list that already has rows keeps them, along with the focused row, while
  loading.

<Canvas of={Stories.InitialLoading} />

<Canvas of={Stories.RetainedLoading} />

To show that a single row is still loading, set `loading` in its
`RowListItemDescriptor`. Its metadata and value are replaced with placeholders,
while its label, description, icon, badge and action stay available. This
example also shows a busy Load more button.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

### Loading more rows

Pass `loadMore` with a `label`, `onAction` and optional `loading` when another
page of data is available. The button keeps its label while busy, and screen
readers hear the same loading announcement as the list, without the existing
rows being read again.

## Empty list

When loading finishes with no rows, the list shows the provider's “No items to
display.” message, and screen readers announce it.

<Canvas of={Stories.Empty} />

## Accessibility

Give the list an `aria-label`, which is required. The list is a single Tab
stop: use the arrow keys to move between rows, and Enter to activate the
focused row. Screen readers announce loading and empty states once,
through a single status message.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Select.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="A fixed-choice field with a popover listbox." />

# Select

`Select` lets people choose one option from a fixed list, shown in a popover
when they press the field. It works with browser forms and autofill.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Options

Pass your data as `items` and a `getItem` function that describes each item.
`getItem` returns an `ItemDescriptor`:

- `id` and `label` are required.
- `description`, `icon`, `badge` and `disabled` are optional.

Options show only this content; you cannot pass custom JSX, class names or
styles.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

## Selected badge

When the selected item has a badge, the field shows it after the label. Screen
readers announce the badge as part of the value, as they do for the option.

<Canvas of={Stories.SelectedBadge} />

## States

`required` and `disabled` behave as they do on a native form control. Set
`readOnly` to prevent the choice from changing; the field stays focusable and
its value is still submitted with the form. Pass a non-empty `error` to mark
the field invalid and show the message; there is no separate `invalid` prop.

Set `loading` while the value is not yet available. The field keeps its shape
and cannot be changed until loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled

To control the value, pass both `value` and `onChange`. `onChange` receives the
selected item from `items`, or `null`, not a DOM event. For an uncontrolled
field, pass `defaultValue` and optionally `onChange`. Controlled and
uncontrolled props cannot be combined.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Blur

`onBlur` reports that focus has left the field, for example to show a
validation error only once the user has moved on. Like `onChange`, it receives
no DOM event. It reports once when focus leaves the whole field: opening the
listbox and choosing an option do not count.

<Canvas of={Stories.Blur} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the field, and screen readers announce the description
and any error with it. The list can be opened and an option chosen entirely
with the keyboard, and focus moves between the field and the list
automatically.

## API

# Skeleton

`Skeleton` is a placeholder shown in place of content while it loads. Set `shape` to `text` (default), `rectangle` or `circle`, and `inlineSize` (width) and `blockSize` (height) to match the content it replaces. Both accept any CSS length, such as `120` or `'60%'`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Shapes} />

## Backgrounds

Place skeletons on the page background or a standard surface. Avoid raised surfaces: in dark mode, a skeleton has the same colour as a raised surface and is not visible on it.

## Accessibility

Pass `label` when the skeleton is the only indication that content is loading; screen readers announce it. Omit `label` when a parent component already announces loading, so the announcement is not repeated. The skeleton is then hidden from assistive technology.

# SkipLink

`SkipLink` lets keyboard users jump past repeated content, such as navigation, straight to the main content. Set `targetId` to the `id` of the page's main content element. The `id` must be unique in the document. Give the target `tabIndex={-1}`, so the link can move focus to it without adding it to the normal Tab order.

If you use `ApplicationShell`, you do not need to add a `SkipLink`: the shell includes one and a focusable main content target.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './TextField.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A flat labelled text input with accessible validation."
/>

# TextField

`TextField` is a single-line text input with a label. Pass `label`, and
optionally `description` and `error`, as props; there are no separate field
parts to assemble.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Description and errors

Use `description` for guidance about what to enter. Pass a non-empty `error`
to mark the field invalid and show the message; there is no separate `invalid`
prop.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

## States

`required`, `disabled` and `readOnly` behave as they do on a native input.

Set `loading` while the value is not yet available. The field keeps its shape,
screen readers announce the provider's loading message, and the field cannot be
edited until loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Required} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled

To control the value, pass both `value` and `onChange`. `onChange` receives the
new string, not a DOM event. For an uncontrolled field, pass `defaultValue` and
optionally `onChange`. Controlled and uncontrolled props cannot be combined.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Blur

`onBlur` reports that focus has left the field, for example to show a
validation error only once the user has moved on. Like `onChange`, it receives
no DOM event.

<Canvas of={Stories.Blur} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the input, and screen readers announce the description
and any error with it. Use `ref` to reach the native input, for example to
focus it.

## API

/>

# Toggle

`Toggle` is a button that switches something on or off, such as a filter.
Use a `Checkbox` instead when the choice belongs in a form.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Pressed state

For an uncontrolled toggle, set `defaultPressed` to choose its starting state.
To control it from your own state, pass both `pressed` and `onChange`.
`onChange` receives the new pressed value. Controlled and uncontrolled props
cannot be combined.

<Canvas of={Stories.Pressed} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while saving a choice. A placeholder replaces the visible label,
and the button keeps its name and width. It cannot be pressed until loading
ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Sizes

`size` accepts `sm`, `md` (default) or `lg`, with minimum heights of 34, 38 and
52px. On touch devices, every size has a target of at least 44px.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

## Disabled

Set `disabled` to prevent the toggle from being pressed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the button, and screen readers announce whether it is
pressed. Use `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to give it a different name, and
`aria-describedby` to add a description. Press Space or Enter to switch it.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './ToggleGroup.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A single-choice segmented control with accessible pressed options."
/>

# ToggleGroup

`ToggleGroup` is a segmented control: a row of connected buttons from which
people choose one option, such as a time period. Pressing the selected option
again clears the selection.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Options

Pass your data as `items` and a `getItem` function that describes each option.
Return a unique `id` and a visible `label`, and optionally a `description`,
`icon`, `badge` or `disabled` flag. Disabled options cannot be selected.

<Canvas of={Stories.DisabledOption} />

## Controlled

For an uncontrolled group, pass `defaultSelected` and optionally `onChange`. To
control the selection from your own state, pass both `selected` and
`onChange`. `onChange` receives the selected item from `items`, or `null` when
the choice is cleared. Controlled and uncontrolled props cannot be combined.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while saving a selection. A slim loading bar replaces each
option's content, while the options keep their size and the selected option
stays highlighted. The selection cannot be changed until loading ends.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Full width

Set `fullWidth` to stretch the group across its container, sharing the width
equally between options, for example in a form.

<Canvas of={Stories.FullWidth} />

## Sizes

`size` accepts `sm` (default), `md` or `lg`, giving the group a minimum height
of 34, 38 or 52px to line up with other controls of the same size. On touch
devices, every option is at least 44px tall, so `sm` and `md` groups grow to
50px.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

## Accessibility

Give each group an `aria-label` that describes the choice. Screen readers
announce whether each option is pressed, and options can be chosen with the
keyboard.

## API

content-typography--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Typography.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Applies Breeze text roles and locale-aware formatting."
/>

# Typography

`Typography` displays text in one of the Breeze text styles, called roles: `money`, `amount`, `heading`, `title`, `body`, `caption`, `label` and `micro`. It also formats currency amounts and dates for the provider's locale.

<Canvas of={Stories.Roles} />

## Numeric figures

The `money` role is designed for figures: digits line up in columns and are spaced slightly tighter. Set `numeric` to give figures in any other role the same treatment; they are also aligned to the end of the line. Text without `numeric` keeps its normal spacing.

<Canvas of={Stories.FiguresAndInterfaceText} />

## Money and dates

Set `format="currency"` or `format="date"` and pass the raw value; it is formatted for the nearest `BreezeProvider` locale.

- Currency uses the `money` role for headline figures, or the `amount` role, a semibold body-size figure, for amounts in rows. The sign follows the locale's placement and uses a true minus character.
- Dates take an ISO calendar date string, typed as `IsoCalendarDate`, such as `2026-03-14`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Formatting} />

### Signs

`sign` controls the sign of a currency amount:

- `auto` (default) shows a sign on negative amounts only.
- `always` also shows `+` on positive amounts.
- `never` hides the sign, for content that shows direction another way.

Zero is never signed, including negative zero and amounts that round to zero, so `-0.004` displays as `£0.00`.

### Dates and time zones

Calendar dates always display the day you pass, whatever the user's time zone. The provider's `timeZone` is not applied to them.

### Invalid values

An invalid currency value throws a `RangeError` naming the problem, rather than displaying a misleading figure:

- `currency` must be a well-formed three-letter code, such as `GBP`. Codes are
  not checked against ISO 4217, so an unknown well-formed code is displayed as
  written.
- `value` must be a finite number. `NaN` and `Infinity` are rejected.
- An invalid `locale` is rejected by `BreezeProvider` before any value is formatted, so it is never reported as a currency error.

Validate or convert untrusted amounts before rendering them. A date that does not exist, such as `2026-02-30`, is displayed as written.

## Loading

Set `loading` while the value is not yet available. A placeholder keeps the text's place.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Accessibility

Each role renders a default element: `heading` renders an `h2`, `title` an `h3`, `body` a `p` and the other roles a `span`. Set `element` to match your page structure, for example `element="h1"` for the page heading. Do not use colour alone to show direction or status.

## API

<ArgTypes />

foundations-breezeprovider--docs.content: import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import * as Stories from './BreezeProvider.stories'; # BreezeProvider `BreezeProvider` supplies the locale, appearance and messages that Breeze UI components need. Render it once, at the root of your application, above every Breeze UI component. A component rendered outside a provider throws an error. ```tsx ``` ## Locale `locale` takes a BCP 47 language tag, such as `en-GB` or `fr-FR`. It sets the language and text direction of everything inside the provider, and the locale used to format numbers, amounts and dates. ### Translating messages Breeze includes English (`en-GB`) text only. To translate it, pass a partial `messages` object; any key you leave out stays in English and is marked as English for screen readers, whatever the page language. Messages cover: - loading and required-field announcements - the `DatePicker` placeholder, Today and clear actions - the `ComboBox` no-match message and the `RowList` empty message - `AppearanceControl` - the close button on overlays - the `Popover` unread indicator - `FileDropZone` instructions and feedback - `DocumentViewer` controls and messages - attachment labels and actions - the `SkipLink` text and the `ApplicationShell` navigation label Other built-in interaction labels are available in English only. ```tsx ``` Some messages contain placeholders that are replaced with values. Keep them in your translations: - `{query}` in `comboBoxNoMatches` is the text the person typed. - In the `FileDropZone` messages, `{types}` is the accepted file types, `{size}` the size limit, `{count}` the number of files added, `{current}` and `{max}` the attachment count and limit, `{fileName}` a rejected file, and `{fileNames}` the files rejected for exceeding the total limit. - In the `DocumentViewer` messages, `{current}` and `{total}` in `documentViewerPage` are the current page and the page count, and `{zoom}` in `documentViewerZoom` is the zoom level as a percentage. For example: ```tsx ``` ## Time zone `timeZone` takes an IANA time-zone name, such as `Europe/London`, used to format times of day. Without it, the browser's time zone is used. The provider throws a `RangeError` for a name the browser does not recognise. **No component formats a time of day yet, so `timeZone` currently has no visible effect.** ```tsx ``` `timeZone` does not affect calendar dates, such as `Typography` with `format="date"`. A calendar date names a day rather than a moment in time, so it always displays the day you pass. ## Appearance Appearance can be `light`, `dark` or `automatic`. The default, `automatic`, follows the operating system's colour scheme, including when it changes while the page is open. To let the provider manage the current choice, set `defaultAppearance`. Use `onAppearanceChange` to save the choice, for example when someone changes it with `AppearanceControl`: ```tsx saveAppearance(appearance)} > ``` To control appearance from your own state, pass both `appearance` and `onAppearanceChange`. `appearance` and `defaultAppearance` cannot be combined. ```tsx ``` The provider does not save the choice. Store it wherever suits your application, such as local storage or a user profile, and pass it back on the next visit. To apply a saved `light` or `dark` choice before your application's JavaScript runs, and so avoid a flash of the wrong colour scheme, set `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on the `` element before the stylesheet loads. You do not need to do this for `automatic`: the stylesheet already follows the operating system before any script runs. ## Overlay portal `Dialog`, `Drawer` and `Popover` stay in your React tree, so context, error boundaries and events work as usual. Only their DOM is rendered in a portal, outside the provider's DOM, in a container the provider adds to `document.body`. To render them somewhere else, such as inside an embedded application, set `portalContainer` to an existing `HTMLElement`. ```tsx ``` The provider adds its own element inside that container and removes it when it unmounts. Overlays keep the provider's styles, locale and text direction wherever they render. `portalContainer` and every overlay trigger must be in the current document. Containers in another document, such as an iframe, or inside a shadow root are not supported. ## Client-side navigation Set `router` when your application uses a client-side router. A `Link` to a same-origin page then calls `router.navigate` with the destination and the link's `transitionTypes`, instead of loading a new page. Your router performs the navigation and can use browser view transitions; see Motion. ```tsx ``` `transitionTypes` defaults to an empty list, so a `navigate` function that takes only the destination works unchanged. External links, downloads, links with another `target`, clicks with a modifier key and links containing a `#` fragment use normal browser navigation. See `Link` for details. ## Confirmations Call `useToast` in a component below the provider to confirm a completed action. Up to three messages are shown at once; further messages wait and appear in the order they were sent. Each message stays on screen for 2.6 seconds. ```tsx import { useToast } from '@motech-development/breeze-ui'; function SaveAction() { const enqueue = useToast(); return ; } ``` Set `toastLimit` to change how many messages are shown at once. Toasts are 288px wide at every screen size and have no action or dismiss button. See `Toast` for details. ## API
